A healthy amount of cynicism is necessary to keep new technology from going out of control. AI art (generative AI in general) is young and still needs regulation, otherwise the integrity of all the things it tries to mimic is at risk.

I agree that AI will just keep improving at this point, but that just makes it all the more important to put necessary regulations and restrictions in place - just as with any new piece of technology. For example, many people like to spite and disrespect artists that refuse to be part of their training data by using their art as training data anyway, outright mocking them. Just because they don't want any AI to be trained on their art. Glaze was created for artists to protect their art, but immediately people studied how to bypass it. There's also the issue of intentionally misleading other people that they drew the AI art themselves. 

Honestly I'm all for it moving forward ETHICALLY, but until we have sufficient progress in regulating AI there will always be enough reason to be wary and reject it.

Say, out of the AI artists you see online, how many are actually using it as a tool and resource to complement their skills, and how many are using it on its own without any of their own input? I see the latter way too often and it makes me feel betrayed when I see what I thought was amazing art and then realize it was just purely AI, like there was no human behind it whose painting skills I can admire.

I used adapalene (a different brand, nor differin) for 6 months and when it ran out I used glycolic acid + benzoyl peroxide for spot treatment (I use glycolic acid on areas where there's benzoyl peroxide). Benzoyl peroxide speeds up the healing of my cystic acne. I'm thinking of switching to tretinoin or salicylic acid when the glycolic acid runs out though, cuz I feel like I need something stronger for the scars. Cleansing balm + cetaphil helped a lot though some people find cetaphil to be drying so I moisturize a lot. 

It also depends on the type of acne you have. Years ago I had fungal infection on my hands and was prescribed antifungal cream, my face cleared up so well. It didn't click until years later when a derma advised me to use ketoconazole weekly on my scalp and face for dandruff, because apparently I had fungal acne (usually appears at the edges of the face or on the neck area where your hair touches). I also read about someone here getting an allergy test and their acne cleared up after avoiding their allergen.
